scenarios.attacker_state: anonymous, valid-or-invalid password submission
scenarios.protocol: invalid credentials are indistinguishable and valid unenrolled login redirects with a final browser session
scenarios.durable_state: invalid login creates no session; successful login creates one session and logout removes it
scenarios.audit: successful login/logout records stable action; rejected login records no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: authenticated browser user with missing CSRF or viewer role
scenarios.protocol: write is rejected with the browser CSRF/viewer contract
scenarios.durable_state: no project mutation occurs
scenarios.audit: rejected CSRF or role write produces no audit row

scenarios.attacker_state: password-validated user carrying only pending MFA state
scenarios.protocol: pending state reaches MFA page, cannot access protected routes, and cancel returns to login
scenarios.durable_state: pending challenge is consumed or invalidated without a final session
scenarios.audit: pending cancel is suppressed; denied protected requests have no audit row

scenarios.attacker_state: invalid-code, expired, or concurrently replayed pending TOTP challenge
scenarios.protocol: invalid or expired TOTP fails without a final session; concurrent valid submissions have one winner
scenarios.durable_state: expired challenges are removed and a valid one-shot TOTP challenge creates exactly one final session
scenarios.audit: invalid TOTP creates no successful factor audit action

scenarios.attacker_state: recently reauthenticated browser session with valid and invalid factor submissions
scenarios.protocol: enrollment requires reauth and valid confirmation; invalid verification is rejected
scenarios.durable_state: confirmed factor persists once and invalidates the old browser session
scenarios.audit: successful enrollment records mfa_totp_enroll; rejected submissions create no successful audit action

scenarios.attacker_state: pending login recovery with invalid, concurrently reused, or replayed code
scenarios.protocol: one valid recovery submission completes login; invalid and replayed submissions fail
scenarios.durable_state: one recovery code is consumed and creates exactly one final session
scenarios.audit: invalid recovery submissions create no successful factor audit action

scenarios.attacker_state: MFA-pending browser with valid or origin-bound passkey ceremony
scenarios.protocol: only the bound browser ceremony completes login; unsupported and wrong-origin attempts remain pending
scenarios.durable_state: valid assertion advances counter and creates one final session; invalid assertion changes neither
scenarios.audit: successful passkey login records mfa_login_factor; rejected ceremony has no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: security-session recovery continuation or regeneration request
scenarios.protocol: excluded from the current runtime matrix; no execution-backed security claim is made
scenarios.durable_state: not asserted by this suite
scenarios.audit: not asserted by this suite

scenarios.attacker_state: authenticated session with fresh, stale, altered, or replayed reauthentication proof
scenarios.protocol: only an active-session factor proof permits a security-sensitive continuation
scenarios.durable_state: reauthentication timestamp changes only on the active valid session
scenarios.audit: successful reauthentication records its stable action; invalid proof has no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: recently reauthenticated browser attempting passkey add, test, mutation, deletion, or MFA disable
scenarios.protocol: mutations require reauth and CSRF; dialog cancellation sends no write; confirmation sends exactly one write
scenarios.durable_state: factor mutation updates the intended factor; last-factor guard and disable invalidate browser state
scenarios.audit: successful mutations use mapped MFA actions; rejected/cancelled requests have no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: admin or non-admin browser with fresh, stale, altered, or replayed reset continuation
scenarios.protocol: only a fresh admin continuation may reset another user; native and no-JS confirmation honor CSRF
scenarios.durable_state: target factors, recovery state, browser sessions, and rate limits are removed atomically
scenarios.audit: one successful mfa_admin_reset action identifies the target; rejected continuations have no action

scenarios.attacker_state: machine bearer credential with no browser session or browser MFA state
scenarios.protocol: valid bearer access succeeds without browser MFA; browser cookie is not an API credential
scenarios.durable_state: API calls do not create browser session or MFA state; reset/disable preserves valid bearer credentials
scenarios.audit: successful mapped API writes audit once; rejected bearer requests have no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: inventory-only route with no dedicated runtime scenario
scenarios.protocol: declarative-only: route remains in the approved inventory but receives no execution-backed claim
scenarios.durable_state: not asserted by this suite
scenarios.audit: not asserted by this suite

scenarios.attacker_state: untrusted client observing MFA responses and test failure artifacts
scenarios.protocol: sensitive MFA responses use no-store and diagnostics retain only approved metadata
scenarios.durable_state: failed requests do not create sessions, factors, or consumed challenge state
scenarios.audit: failed sensitive requests have no successful audit action

scenarios.attacker_state: anonymous browser begins login through the process-local TLS provider fixture
scenarios.protocol: valid authorization-code login binds state, nonce, and S256 PKCE before issuing one browser session
scenarios.durable_state: one transaction is consumed and one linked local identity and browser session exist
scenarios.audit: successful OIDC login records one stable factor action; start alone creates no session or audit row

scenarios.attacker_state: callback with altered transaction bindings or a reused authorization response
scenarios.protocol: state, nonce, PKCE, and replay mismatches fail before a second exchange or session
scenarios.durable_state: rejected or replayed callbacks leave no new user, session, audit row, or reusable transaction
scenarios.audit: rejected callbacks record no successful factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: callback backed by a token with a wrong issuer, audience, signature, expiry, or nonce
scenarios.protocol: the local TLS verifier rejects every failed trust binding with a generic no-store response
scenarios.durable_state: unverified identity data creates no user, identity link, session, or successful audit row
scenarios.audit: verifier failures record no successful factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: verified fixture identity matches an existing local email or presents invalid identity claims
scenarios.protocol: only verified, valid claims can first-link an existing local account
scenarios.durable_state: a valid link preserves the local user while invalid claims create no identity or session
scenarios.audit: only a successful linked login records the stable factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: two first-login resolutions race for the same verified fixture identity
scenarios.protocol: concurrent first login converges on one durable local user after a real TLS callback path
scenarios.durable_state: one identity link and one local user win the first-link race
scenarios.audit: the successful callback path retains the normal single factor audit contract

scenarios.attacker_state: verified fixture groups map a first login or downgrade an existing local role
scenarios.protocol: configured exact group mapping applies role authority without accepting unverified data
scenarios.durable_state: a role downgrade removes existing browser sessions before the synchronized role is retained
scenarios.audit: only successful mapped login uses the stable factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: anonymous, stale, replayed, alternate-session, or alternate-subject reauthentication attempt
scenarios.protocol: reauthentication requires the protected bound session and the same current provider subject
scenarios.durable_state: only the bound active session can refresh and resume its continuation; no callback creates a new session
scenarios.audit: rejected reauthentication attempts record no successful factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: provider discovery or token endpoint is unavailable after local startup
scenarios.protocol: the OIDC start returns a generic failure while password login stays available
scenarios.durable_state: outage creates no browser credential and preserves existing sessions and bearer API access
scenarios.audit: outage rejection records no successful OIDC factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: provider failures, verifier cache reuse, and test-runner failure diagnostics
scenarios.protocol: provider failures remain generic and the local TLS cache never retains request context values
scenarios.durable_state: failed exchange creates no local authentication state and test artifacts retain only approved metadata
scenarios.audit: failed OIDC exchanges record no successful factor action

scenarios.attacker_state: browser reaches an OIDC path while the optional provider is disabled
scenarios.protocol: all OIDC paths remain absent and password login exposes no SSO action
scenarios.durable_state: disabled routing creates no OIDC transaction, local user, session, or audit state
scenarios.audit: disabled OIDC requests record no successful action

scenarios.attacker_state: concurrent database consumers for challenge, factor, recovery, and reset state
scenarios.protocol: bounded parity suite observes one winner for guarded consumption and valid pending-to-final transition
scenarios.durable_state: migration, binary credentials, expiry, recovery, reset rollback, and API token state match contract
scenarios.audit: successful mapped browser actions retain stable audit semantics

scenarios.attacker_state: concurrent database consumers for challenge, factor, recovery, and reset state
scenarios.protocol: bounded parity suite observes one winner for guarded consumption and valid pending-to-final transition
scenarios.durable_state: migration, binary credentials, expiry, recovery, reset rollback, and API token state match contract
scenarios.audit: successful mapped browser actions retain stable audit semantics

exclusions.reason: this suite exercises the app boundary, not a hostile server or endpoint takeover

exclusions.threat: host, browser, network, or identity-provider compromise
exclusions.reason: outside the isolated application and database attack contract

exclusions.threat: requiring MFA for bearer API tokens
exclusions.reason: API tokens are deliberately MFA-exempt machine credentials and browser MFA reset/disable preserves them
